components.note: 手 (hand) — the bottom 手 is a hand — 举 is lifting with the hands, as in 举行.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 有问题的同学请举手。
example.pinyin: Yǒu wèntí de tóngxué qǐng jǔshǒu.
example.english: Students with questions, please raise your hand.
example.fact: Humans, along with gibbons and a few other primates, have a shoulder joint flexible enough to rotate the arm a full 360 degrees overhead, an adaptation originally suited for swinging through trees, a movement called brachiation. That same shoulder mobility is why humans can throw overhand and raise an arm straight up, motions most other mammals cannot perform.

examples.hanzi: 同意的请举手。
examples.pinyin: Tóngyì de qǐng jǔshǒu.
examples.english: Those in favor, please raise your hand.

examples.hanzi: 他举手投降，不再反抗。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǔshǒu tóuxiáng, bù zài fǎnkàng.
examples.english: He raised his hands in surrender and stopped resisting.

components.note: 手 (hand) — the bottom 手 is a hand — 举 is lifting with the hands, as in 举行.
止 (stop) — a picture of a foot planted on the ground: where the foot stops. Seen in 步 step (two feet) and 正 correct.

example.hanzi: 她的举止一直很优雅。
example.pinyin: Tā de jǔzhǐ yīzhí hěn yōuyǎ.
example.english: Her manner has always been graceful.
example.fact: Emily Post's 1922 book 'Etiquette' became a best-seller by codifying rules of proper social conduct for a rapidly changing American middle class, and her name became so associated with manners that 'an Emily Post' is still used informally to describe someone with impeccable bearing. The book has been revised many times since and remains in print a century later.

examples.hanzi: 他的举止很得体，给人留下好印象。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jǔzhǐ hěn détǐ, gěi rén liúxià hǎo yìnxiàng.
examples.english: His manners were appropriate and left a good impression.

examples.hanzi: 这个人举止奇怪，大家都有点害怕。
examples.pinyin: Zhège rén jǔzhǐ qíguài, dàjiā dōu yǒudiǎn hàipà.
examples.english: This person behaves strangely, and everybody is a bit afraid.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a lone person under a roof: alone, few; also in 家 home, 安 peace.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 妇 is a married woman.
彐 (hand) — 彐 is a hand holding a broom (the traditional 婦 had 帚), so a married woman who keeps house.

example.hanzi: 她年轻时就成了寡妇,独自抚养三个孩子。
example.pinyin: Tā niánqīng shí jiù chéngle guǎfu, dúzì fǔyǎng sān gè háizi.
example.english: She became a widow while still young and raised three children alone.
example.fact: The black widow spider takes its English name from a once-common belief that females always devour their male mates after courtship, but field studies show this actually happens in only a small fraction of encounters and is far more common under crowded laboratory conditions than in the wild. Males of some widow spider species have even evolved courtship behaviors that reduce their odds of being eaten.

examples.hanzi: 这位寡妇一个人住在山脚下的小屋里。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi guǎfu yī gè rén zhù zài shān jiǎo xià de xiǎowū lǐ.
examples.english: This widow lives alone in a small hut at the foot of the mountain.

examples.hanzi: 邻居们常常帮助那位年老的寡妇。
examples.pinyin: Línjūmen chángcháng bāngzhù nà wèi niánlǎo de guǎfu.
examples.english: The neighbors often help that elderly widow.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摇 is to shake or rock.
䍃 (yáo) — same sound — 摇 is yáo; 䍃 also sounds out 谣 yáo and 遥 yáo.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摆 is to arrange or swing with the hands.
罢 (bà) — near sound — 摆 is bǎi, matching 罢.

example.hanzi: 大风中,树枝不停地摇摆。
example.pinyin: Dà fēng zhōng, shùzhī bùtíng de yáobǎi.
example.english: In the strong wind, the tree branches kept swaying.
example.fact: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington State famously collapsed in 1940 after wind caused it to twist and sway with such large oscillations that engineers captured the structure flexing dramatically on film before it tore apart. The disaster became a textbook case in engineering for how resonance and aerodynamic flutter can destroy even a well-built structure.

examples.hanzi: 小船在海浪中左右摇摆。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎochuán zài hǎilàng zhōng zuǒyòu yáobǎi.
examples.english: The little boat swayed from side to side on the waves.

examples.hanzi: 他在两个选择之间摇摆不定。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài liǎng gè xuǎnzé zhījiān yáobǎi bù dìng.
examples.english: He wavers between the two options.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 竹子的生长速度非常快。
example.pinyin: Zhúzi de shēngzhǎng sùdù fēicháng kuài.
example.english: Bamboo's growth rate is extremely fast.
example.fact: Certain species of bamboo are the fastest-growing plants on Earth, and a Guinness World Record documents a specimen in Japan that grew 91 centimeters — nearly three feet — in a single day. This rapid growth comes from pre-formed nodes in the shoot that expand rather than dividing new cells from scratch, letting the plant lengthen almost like unfolding an accordion.

examples.hanzi: 这种花在温暖的地方生长得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng huā zài wēnnuǎn de dìfang shēngzhǎng de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This kind of flower grows well in warm places.

examples.hanzi: 他生长在一个小渔村里。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēngzhǎng zài yī gè xiǎo yúcūn lǐ.
examples.english: He grew up in a small fishing village.

components.note: 木 (wood) — wooden things: 桌, 板, 桥; 架 is a wooden frame or rack.
加 (jiā) is a near sound match for jià; also in 驾 jià and 嘉 jiā.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 书都放在那个木头架子上。
example.pinyin: Shū dōu fàng zài nàge mùtou jiàzi shàng.
example.english: All the books are placed on that wooden shelf.
example.fact: The Dewey Decimal System, created by Melvil Dewey in 1876, organizes library shelves by assigning every subject a numeric code between 000 and 999, letting books on related topics sit physically near each other no matter how large the library is. More than 200,000 libraries worldwide still use some version of the system today to decide exactly where a book belongs on the shelf.

examples.hanzi: 他穿衣服很随便，一点架子也没有。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān yīfu hěn suíbiàn, yīdiǎn jiàzi yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: He dresses casually and puts on no airs at all.

examples.hanzi: 厨房里的架子上摆满了调料瓶。
examples.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ de jiàzi shàng bǎi mǎn le tiáoliào píng.
examples.english: The shelf in the kitchen is full of spice jars.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 石 as in 破 break, 砖 brick: hard things colliding — 碰 is to bump into.
並 (bìng) — loose hint — 碰 is pèng; 並 (bìng) also sounds out 拼 pīn and 屏 píng.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 我们明天下午在图书馆门口碰头。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān xiàwǔ zài túshūguǎn ménkǒu pèngtóu.
example.english: Let's meet at the library entrance tomorrow afternoon.
example.fact: At the Large Hadron Collider near Geneva, protons are accelerated to 99.9999991 percent of the speed of light before being made to meet head-on inside detectors, producing collisions energetic enough to have revealed the Higgs boson in 2012. Each proton bunch crosses another roughly 40 million times per second inside the ring, though only a tiny fraction of those crossings produce a meaningful collision.

examples.hanzi: 大家下班后在老地方碰头。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā xiàbān hòu zài lǎo dìfang pèngtóu.
examples.english: After work everyone will meet at the usual place.

examples.hanzi: 我们先碰头商量一下，再做决定。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān pèngtóu shāngliang yīxià, zài zuò juédìng.
examples.english: Let's meet and discuss it first before we decide.

components.note: 甲 (jiǎ) — shell, armour, first of the heavenly stems; as a part it sounds out 钾 jiǎ and 胛 jiǎ.
木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 桌, 桥; 板 is a plank or board.
反 (fǎn) is a near sound match (-an); same part in 饭 fàn and 版 bǎn.

example.hanzi: 乘客们站在甲板上看日落。
example.pinyin: Chéngkèmen zhàn zài jiǎbǎn shàng kàn rìluò.
example.english: The passengers stood on the deck watching the sunset.
example.fact: The flight deck of the USS Gerald R. Ford, the largest aircraft carrier ever built, spans more than 4.5 acres, roughly the size of three football fields, and can support the launch and recovery of more than 75 aircraft. Catapults built into the deck accelerate jets from a standstill to over 150 miles per hour in about two seconds.

examples.hanzi: 海鸥落在了船的甲板上。
examples.pinyin: Hǎi'ōu luò zài le chuán de jiǎbǎn shàng.
examples.english: A seagull landed on the ship's deck.

examples.hanzi: 风很大，水手们赶紧跑回甲板下面。
examples.pinyin: Fēng hěn dà, shuǐshǒumen gǎnjǐn pǎo huí jiǎbǎn xiàmiàn.
examples.english: The wind was strong, so the sailors rushed below deck.

components.note: 化 (change) — one person 亻 beside an upside-down person 匕 — a change of state; 化 is to change, as in 文化 and 变化.
女 (woman) — marks women, as in 妈, 姐, 好; 妆 is make-up.
丬 (a form of 爿) hints at the sound: 妆 zhuāng, close to 壮 zhuàng, 状 zhuàng and 装 zhuāng.
口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 这家商场新开了一个化妆品专柜。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngchǎng xīn kāile yī gè huàzhuāngpǐn zhuānguì.
example.english: This mall just opened a new cosmetics counter.
example.fact: Archaeologists have found kohl eyeliner in ancient Egyptian tombs dating back roughly 4,000 years, worn by both men and women partly for its believed protection against eye infections and the sun's glare along the Nile. Chemical analysis of surviving samples shows the Egyptians combined lead-based minerals in ways some modern researchers argue may have had genuine antibacterial effects, despite the toxicity of the lead itself.

examples.hanzi: 她的包里装满了化妆品。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bāo lǐ zhuāng mǎn le huàzhuāngpǐn.
examples.english: Her bag is full of cosmetics.

examples.hanzi: 买化妆品之前，要先看看成分表。
examples.pinyin: Mǎi huàzhuāngpǐn zhīqián, yào xiān kànkan chéngfèn biǎo.
examples.english: Before buying cosmetics, check the ingredient list first.

components.note: 氵 (water) — crossing a river; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
度 (dù) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 我们坐船渡过了河。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò chuán dùguò le hé.
example.english: We crossed the river by boat.
example.fact: 渡 means crossing water, as in 渡口 (ferry crossing), 摆渡 (ferry), and figuratively 渡过难关 (get through a hard time).

examples.hanzi: 他们坐渡船过江。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zuò dùchuán guò jiāng.
examples.english: They crossed the river by ferry.

examples.hanzi: 他们划着船渡过了小河。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen huá zhe chuán dùguò le xiǎohé.
examples.english: They rowed a boat across the small river.

components.note: 力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.hanzi: 中国队最终力克强敌,赢得了冠军。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó duì zuìzhōng lìkè qiángdí, yíngdéle guànjūn.
example.english: The Chinese team finally prevailed over a strong opponent and won the championship.
example.fact: In the 1980 Winter Olympics, a team of American college players and amateurs defeated the heavily favored Soviet Union hockey team 4-3, a result so unlikely it became known as the 'Miracle on Ice.' The Soviet squad had won the previous four Olympic gold medals and had beaten an NHL All-Star team just weeks earlier, making the upset one of the most cited comebacks in sports history.

examples.hanzi: 他在决赛中力克对手，夺得了金牌。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài juésài zhōng lìkè duìshǒu, duóde le jīnpái.
examples.english: He beat his opponent in the final and won the gold medal.

examples.hanzi: 我们队在加时赛中力克了去年的冠军。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen duì zài jiāshísài zhōng lìkè le qùnián de guànjūn.
examples.english: Our team defeated last year's champions in overtime.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁; 镇 first meant to weigh down with metal.
真 (zhēn) — near sound — 镇 is zhèn; 真 also sounds out 慎 shèn and 填 tián.
青 (qīng) hints at the -ing rhyme; same part in 清 请 情 晴 精. The 争 (contend) half is not a reliable clue.

example.hanzi: 面对突发情况,她始终保持镇静。
example.pinyin: Miànduì tūfā qíngkuàng, tā shǐzhōng bǎochí zhènjìng.
example.english: Facing the sudden situation, she remained calm throughout.
example.fact: The vagus nerve, running from the brainstem down through the chest and abdomen, plays a central role in slowing the heart rate and lowering blood pressure after a stressful moment, which is why slow, deliberate breathing can measurably calm the body. Free divers deliberately train this response through breath-holding practice, letting some elite athletes drop their heart rate below 30 beats per minute while submerged.

examples.hanzi: 出了事故，他马上镇静下来打电话求助。
examples.pinyin: Chū le shìgù, tā mǎshàng zhènjìng xiàlái dǎ diànhuà qiúzhù.
examples.english: After the accident, he calmed down immediately and called for help.

examples.hanzi: 请大家保持镇静，不要慌。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā bǎochí zhènjìng, bù yào huāng.
examples.english: Everyone please stay calm and don't panic.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
阝 (hill, from 阜) on the left — marks slopes and barriers, as in 院, 陆, 附, 阶; 障 is a barrier.
章 (zhāng) hints at the sound: 障 zhàng is close, as in 彰 zhāng.

example.hanzi: 政府承诺保障公民的基本权利。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ chéngnuò bǎozhàng gōngmín de jīběn quánlì.
example.english: The government promised to safeguard citizens' basic rights.
example.fact: Germany created the world's first modern social insurance system in 1889 under Chancellor Otto von Bismarck, guaranteeing old-age pensions to workers starting at age 70. The program was in part a strategic move to undercut the growing socialist movement by having the state itself safeguard workers' welfare, and it became the model many other countries later adapted into their own social security systems.

examples.hanzi: 这份保险能保障你的家人的生活。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bǎoxiǎn néng bǎozhàng nǐ de jiārén de shēnghuó.
examples.english: This insurance can safeguard your family's livelihood.

examples.hanzi: 法律是我们权利的重要保障。
examples.pinyin: Fǎlǜ shì wǒmen quánlì de zhòngyào bǎozhàng.
examples.english: The law is an important guarantee of our rights.

meanings: to dispatch sb to do sth

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).

example.hanzi: 他靠看书打发漫长的火车旅程。
example.pinyin: Tā kào kànshū dǎfa màncháng de huǒchē lǚchéng.
example.english: He passed the long train journey by reading books.
example.fact: The Pony Express, which operated for only about eighteen months in 1860 and 1861, used relays of riders and horses to carry mail nearly 2,000 miles between Missouri and California in nominally ten days. It was made obsolete almost overnight once the transcontinental telegraph line was completed in October 1861, letting messages travel the same distance in minutes instead.

examples.hanzi: 你先打发他走，我一会儿再处理。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān dǎfa tā zǒu, wǒ yīhuǐr zài chǔlǐ.
examples.english: Send him away first, and I'll deal with it in a moment.

examples.hanzi: 周末在家没事做，就看看电视打发时间。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò zài jiā méi shì zuò, jiù kànkan diànshì dǎfa shíjiān.
examples.english: With nothing to do at home on the weekend, I just watch TV to pass the time.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 呼, 吃, 喝; 吸 is to breathe in.
及 (jí) is a loose sound hint for xī; same part in 级 jí and 极 jí.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.

example.hanzi: 植物通过根部吸收水分和养分。
example.pinyin: Zhíwù tōngguò gēnbù xīshōu shuǐfèn hé yǎngfèn.
example.english: Plants absorb water and nutrients through their roots.
example.fact: Activated charcoal owes its powerful absorbing ability to an enormous internal surface area — a single gram can have a surface area exceeding 1,000 square meters, roughly the size of a football field, once its microscopic pores are unfolded. That vast surface lets it bind large quantities of toxins and gases, which is why it's used both in emergency-room poison treatment and in household water filters.

examples.hanzi: 海绵可以吸收很多水分。
examples.pinyin: Hǎimián kěyǐ xīshōu hěn duō shuǐfèn.
examples.english: A sponge can absorb a lot of water.

examples.hanzi: 他善于吸收别人的好意见。
examples.pinyin: Tā shànyú xīshōu biéren de hǎo yìjiàn.
examples.english: He is good at taking in other people's good ideas.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.
言 (speech) — praise is spoken; the radical of 说 and 语 in its full form.
兴 (xīng) here stands in for an older sound part: the old form 譽 had 與 (yǔ), which gave yù.

example.hanzi: 这项发现为他赢得了国际名誉。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng fāxiàn wèi tā yíngdéle guójì míngyù.
example.english: This discovery earned him international renown.
example.fact: Alfred Nobel is said to have been motivated to establish the Nobel Prizes partly after reading a premature obituary that a French newspaper mistakenly published about him in 1888, describing him harshly as a 'merchant of death' for inventing dynamite. He revised his will soon after to fund prizes recognizing benefits to humanity, reshaping how his reputation would be remembered after his actual death in 1896.

examples.hanzi: 他很在乎自己的名誉。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn zàihu zìjǐ de míngyù.
examples.english: He cares a lot about his reputation.

examples.hanzi: 法院还给了这位教授清白和名誉。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn huán gěi le zhè wèi jiàoshòu qīngbái hé míngyù.
examples.english: The court restored the professor's innocence and honor.

components.note: 夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.
罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and catching: 罗, 罚, 罪; 置 first meant to set a net, then to place.
直 (zhí) is a near sound match for zhì; same part in 值 zhí and 植 zhí.

example.hanzi: 这批过期药品必须妥善处置。
example.pinyin: Zhè pī guòqī yàopǐn bìxū tuǒshàn chǔzhì.
example.english: This batch of expired medicine must be properly disposed of.
example.fact: Finland's Onkalo repository, carved more than 400 meters into bedrock, is designed to handle spent nuclear fuel safely for at least 100,000 years, making it one of the longest-planned engineering projects in human history. Its copper canisters and clay buffers are meant to isolate the waste from groundwater long after any current human institution could be expected to still exist to monitor it.

examples.hanzi: 这件事由经理亲自处置。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yóu jīnglǐ qīnzì chǔzhì.
examples.english: The manager will personally handle this matter.

examples.hanzi: 违规的员工受到了严厉的处置。
examples.pinyin: Wéiguī de yuángōng shòudào le yánlì de chǔzhì.
examples.english: The employee who broke the rules was severely dealt with.

components.note: 爫 (hand) — a hand 爫 reaching down to a tree 木 to pick its fruit or leaves — to gather, as in 采访.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 公司决定采用新的生产技术。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī juédìng cǎiyòng xīn de shēngchǎn jìshù.
example.english: The company decided to adopt the new production technology.
example.fact: The QWERTY keyboard layout was adopted for early typewriters in the 1870s partly to slow typists down and reduce jamming in mechanical keys, yet it remains the dominant layout on computer keyboards worldwide even though the mechanical constraint that shaped it disappeared decades ago. Alternative layouts like Dvorak, designed to be faster, have never displaced it because of how deeply the original choice became entrenched.

examples.hanzi: 这所学校采用小班教学。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào cǎiyòng xiǎobān jiàoxué.
examples.english: This school uses small-class teaching.

examples.hanzi: 编辑采用了我的意见，修改了标题。
examples.pinyin: Biānjí cǎiyòng le wǒ de yìjiàn, xiūgǎi le biāotí.
examples.english: The editor adopted my suggestion and changed the title.

meanings: a type of literature consisting mainly of short sketches

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — brush shafts were bamboo; also in 笑 smile, 筷 chopsticks.
毛 (hair) — the brush hair at the tip; 笔 is brush and pen.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.

example.hanzi: 上课时她认真做笔记。
example.pinyin: Shàngkè shí tā rènzhēn zuò bǐjì.
example.english: During class, she takes notes carefully.
example.fact: Leonardo da Vinci filled more than 13,000 surviving pages of notebooks with sketches, mirror-written observations, and technical designs, covering subjects from human anatomy to flying machines centuries before powered flight existed. He often wrote right to left in a script only readable when held up to a mirror, a habit some historians attribute to his being left-handed rather than any attempt at secrecy.

examples.hanzi: 我借了同学的笔记来复习。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiè le tóngxué de bǐjì lái fùxí.
examples.english: I borrowed my classmate's notes to review.

examples.hanzi: 你可以用电脑记笔记，也可以用手写。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng diànnǎo jì bǐjì, yě kěyǐ yòng shǒuxiě.
examples.english: You can take notes on a computer or by hand.

components.note: 首 (head, first) — a picture of a head with hair on top, which became the word for first and chief: 首先, 元首, also a measure for songs.
阝 (city) — right-side 阝 is 邑 city — 都 is a capital, as in 首都; compare 那, 邮.
者 (zhě) — loose hint — 都 is dū; 者 also sounds out 赌 dǔ and 堵 dǔ, a dū/dǔ series.

example.hanzi: 巴黎是法国的首都。
example.pinyin: Bālí shì Fàguó de shǒudū.
example.english: Paris is the capital of France.
example.fact: Naypyidaw became Myanmar's capital in 2005 after the military government relocated the seat of government there almost overnight from Yangon, building a sprawling, purpose-designed city whose twenty-lane highways today carry only a fraction of the traffic they were built for. By contrast, La Paz, Bolivia's administrative capital, sits at about 3,650 meters above sea level, making it the highest capital city in the world.

examples.hanzi: 你知道日本的首都是哪个城市吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào Rìběn de shǒudū shì nǎge chéngshì ma?
examples.english: Do you know which city is the capital of Japan?

examples.hanzi: 首都的交通一直很拥挤。
examples.pinyin: Shǒudū de jiāotōng yīzhí hěn yōngjǐ.
examples.english: Traffic in the capital is always crowded.

components.note: 广 (house) — the cover on top, as in 店 shop. It marks a room or hall where people celebrate.
大 (big) — the part inside the house. Dictionary story: a great (大) event in a house; 庆祝 celebrate. Memory aid, as 庆 is simplified from 慶.
幸 (luck) — often read as an old picture of shackles; 'luck' is escaping punishment. The dictionary story (one alive 土, one dead 干) is a memory aid.
土 (earth) — the top. Memory aid: the one standing on solid ground 土 is the lucky one — 幸运, 幸福.

example.hanzi: 大家都庆幸这次事故没有人员伤亡。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu qìngxìng zhè cì shìgù méiyǒu rényuán shāngwáng.
example.english: Everyone was relieved that no one was hurt in this accident.
example.fact: A four-leaf clover occurs naturally in only about one in five thousand clover plants, a rarity caused by a recessive genetic trait, a developmental error, or environmental stress on the plant. Finding one is rare enough that some clover farms in Ireland now deliberately breed and sell them, guaranteeing customers the luck-seeking rarity that would otherwise take patient searching through an entire field.

examples.hanzi: 我很庆幸当时带了雨伞。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn qìngxìng dāngshí dài le yǔsǎn.
examples.english: I'm glad I brought an umbrella then.

examples.hanzi: 他庆幸自己没有错过那趟火车。
examples.pinyin: Tā qìngxìng zìjǐ méiyǒu cuòguò nà tàng huǒchē.
examples.english: He felt lucky he hadn't missed that train.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water: 河, 深, 浅; 测 was measuring the depth of water.
则 (zé) is close to cè; same part in 侧 cè and 厕 cè.
马 (horse) — horses: 骑, 驾, 骄; 验 first meant testing a horse, then any test.
佥 (qiān) gives the -ian rhyme; same part in 险 xiǎn, 检 jiǎn, 脸 liǎn, 签 qiān.

example.hanzi: 老师下周要进行一次数学测验。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī xià zhōu yào jìnxíng yī cì shùxué cèyàn.
example.english: The teacher will give a math test next week.
example.fact: In 1950, mathematician Alan Turing proposed what became known as the Turing Test, in which a human judge holds text conversations with both a person and a machine and tries to tell which is which; if the judge cannot reliably tell them apart, the machine is said to have passed. More than seventy years later, the test remains a widely cited benchmark for discussing machine intelligence, even as researchers debate how meaningful passing it actually is.

examples.hanzi: 下午有一个英语听力测验。
examples.pinyin: Xiàwǔ yǒu yī gè Yīngyǔ tīnglì cèyàn.
examples.english: There is an English listening test this afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 这个小测验可以测出你的性格类型。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo cèyàn kěyǐ cè chū nǐ de xìnggé lèixíng.
examples.english: This little quiz can tell what personality type you are.

components.note: 医 (doctor) — simplified from 醫, which had 酉 (medicinal wine, as in 酒) at the bottom; the box 匚 and arrow 矢 remain.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound) — as in 险, 阳, 阴: a walled yard.
完 (wán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; also in 玩 wán.

example.hanzi: 他从医学院毕业后成为一名外科医生。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng yīxuéyuàn bìyè hòu chéngwéi yī míng wàikē yīshēng.
example.english: After graduating from medical school, he became a surgeon.
example.fact: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine, which opened in 1893, was the first American medical school to require applicants to already hold a college degree and to admit women on equal terms with men from its founding. Its four-year curriculum, combining lectures with hands-on clinical training in a teaching hospital, became the model that most modern medical schools in the United States still follow.

examples.hanzi: 她从小就梦想考进医学院。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù mèngxiǎng kǎo jìn yīxuéyuàn.
examples.english: She has dreamed of getting into medical school since childhood.

examples.hanzi: 这所医学院的毕业生都很受欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ yīxuéyuàn de bìyèshēng dōu hěn shòu huānyíng.
examples.english: Graduates of this medical school are all in demand.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.
示 (show) — an altar, a table for offerings; as the radical 礻 it marks rites and spirits: 神, 礼, 福, 社, 祝.

example.hanzi: 工程师现场演示了新产品的功能。
example.pinyin: Gōngchéngshī xiànchǎng yǎnshìle xīn chǎnpǐn de gōngnéng.
example.english: The engineer demonstrated the new product's features on site.
example.fact: Alexander Graham Bell gave one of the telephone's first major public demonstrations at the 1876 Centennial Exhibition in Philadelphia, where Emperor Pedro II of Brazil reportedly listened through the receiver and exclaimed, 'My God, it talks!' The device drew relatively little attention at first among the exhibition's thousands of exhibits, and it took several more years of demonstrations before telephone service began spreading commercially.

examples.hanzi: 老师用幻灯片演示了实验的步骤。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī yòng huàndēngpiàn yǎnshì le shíyàn de bùzhòu.
examples.english: The teacher demonstrated the experiment steps with slides.

examples.hanzi: 你能给我演示一下这个软件怎么用吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng gěi wǒ yǎnshì yīxià zhège ruǎnjiàn zěnme yòng ma?
examples.english: Can you show me how to use this software?

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 做 do; 他 is "he" (or other).
也 (yě) is only a loose sound hint for tā; the sibling 她 tā (she) shares it with 女 for woman.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 我周末要去他家吃饭。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò yào qù tā jiā chīfàn.
example.english: I'm going to his house for dinner this weekend.
example.fact: The Mosuo people, living around Lugu Lake on the border of China's Yunnan and Sichuan provinces, are one of the few societies where family lineage and property pass through the mother's line rather than the father's, and children traditionally grow up in their mother's home rather than moving in with a spouse's family. Anthropologists have studied Mosuo kinship extensively because their arrangement of home and family challenges assumptions common to many other cultures about what a household must look like.

examples.hanzi: 他家离学校很近，走路十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn, zǒulù shí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: His home is very close to school, a ten-minute walk.

examples.hanzi: 你知道他家的电话号码吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào tā jiā de diànhuà hàomǎ ma?
examples.english: Do you know his home phone number?

components.note: 阝 (city, place) — right-side 阝 is 邑 (city or place), as in 都, 那, 邻; 邮 was a relay post station.
由 (yóu) — same sound — 邮 is yóu, like 由; 由 also sounds out 油 yóu.

example.hanzi: 我去邮局寄信。
example.pinyin: Wǒ qù yóujú jì xìn.
example.english: I'm going to the post office to send a letter.
example.fact: 邮 gives 邮局 (post office), 邮票 (stamp), 邮件 (mail, email) and 邮寄 (to post). It originally meant a relay station.

examples.hanzi: 我把包裹邮寄给他。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ bāoguǒ yóujì gěi tā.
examples.english: I mailed the parcel to him.

examples.hanzi: 你的邮箱地址是多少？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de yóuxiāng dìzhǐ shì duōshao?
examples.english: What is your email address?

components.note: 角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.
刂 (knife, 立刀旁) — cutting, as in 别 separate, 刻 carve, 剪 cut.
咅 (pōu) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 部 bù, 陪 péi and 培 péi.

example.hanzi: 医学生需要在实验课上解剖青蛙。
example.pinyin: Yīxuéshēng xūyào zài shíyàn kè shàng jiěpōu qīngwā.
example.english: Medical students need to dissect frogs in lab class.
example.fact: Andreas Vesalius's 1543 book 'De Humani Corporis Fabrica,' based on his own dissections rather than centuries-old texts, corrected numerous errors that had persisted since the ancient physician Galen and is considered the founding work of modern human anatomy. Vesalius reportedly obtained some of his cadavers by retrieving the bodies of executed criminals from gallows outside Padua at night.

examples.hanzi: 医生解剖了那具尸体，找到了死因。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jiěpōu le nà jù shītǐ, zhǎodào le sǐyīn.
examples.english: The doctor dissected the body and found the cause of death.

examples.hanzi: 这本书从解剖的角度解释了人体的结构。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū cóng jiěpōu de jiǎodù jiěshì le réntǐ de jiégòu.
examples.english: This book explains the human body's structure from the perspective of anatomy.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — marks cutting and punishing, as in 别, 刻, 划; 刑 is a punishment.
开 (a worn-down 幵) gives the sound exactly: 刑 xíng, also in 形 xíng and 型 xíng.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 这是一起严重的刑事案件。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yī qǐ yánzhòng de xíngshì ànjiàn.
example.english: This is a serious criminal case.
example.fact: The requirement that police inform suspects of their right to remain silent and to an attorney comes from the 1966 U.S. Supreme Court case Miranda v. Arizona, after which the now-familiar 'Miranda warning' became standard practice in American criminal law enforcement. Ernesto Miranda, whose confession had been thrown out because he was never told of these rights, was nonetheless convicted at a second trial using other evidence.

examples.hanzi: 这起案件已经转为刑事调查。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ ànjiàn yǐjīng zhuǎn wéi xíngshì diàochá.
examples.english: This case has turned into a criminal investigation.

examples.hanzi: 他是一名刑事律师，专门处理犯罪案件。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yī míng xíngshì lǜshī, zhuānmén chǔlǐ fànzuì ànjiàn.
examples.english: He is a criminal lawyer who specializes in crime cases.

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.
阝 (hill, from 阜) on the left — marks slopes and barriers, as in 院, 陆, 附, 阶; 障 is a barrier.
章 (zhāng) hints at the sound: 障 zhàng is close, as in 彰 zhāng.

example.hanzi: 警方在路口设置了路障。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zài lùkǒu shèzhìle lùzhàng.
example.english: The police set up a roadblock at the intersection.
example.fact: The Berlin Wall, construction of which began in August 1961, was one of history's most extreme roadblocks, eventually stretching about 155 kilometers and dividing a single city with guard towers, trenches, and fortified fencing rather than a single barrier. It stood for 28 years until it was opened in November 1989 and was largely dismantled within the following year.

examples.hanzi: 前方有路障，车辆请绕行。
examples.pinyin: Qiánfāng yǒu lùzhàng, chēliàng qǐng ràoxíng.
examples.english: There is a roadblock ahead, so vehicles please take a detour.

examples.hanzi: 示威者在街上设了路障。
examples.pinyin: Shìwēizhě zài jiē shàng shè le lùzhàng.
examples.english: The protesters set up a barricade on the street.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.
目 (eye) — 目 marks the eye and looking, as in 看, 眼, 睛; 瞧 is to look.
焦 (jiāo) — near sound — 瞧 is qiáo; 焦 also sounds out 憔 qiáo.

example.hanzi: 你别得意,咱们走着瞧。
example.pinyin: Nǐ bié déyì, zánmen zǒuzheqiáo.
example.english: Don't get too pleased with yourself — let's wait and see.
example.fact: In quantum mechanics, the Schrödinger's cat thought experiment, proposed in 1935, imagines a cat in a sealed box whose fate is tied to a random atomic decay, described mathematically as a superposition of both alive and dead states until someone opens the box and observes the outcome. Erwin Schrödinger devised the scenario not to describe a real physical possibility but to highlight how strange it is to take quantum superposition literally at the scale of everyday objects.

examples.hanzi: 这次你赢了，走着瞧吧，下次我不会输。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì nǐ yíng le, zǒuzheqiáo ba, xià cì wǒ bù huì shū.
examples.english: You won this time, but just wait and see, I won't lose next time.

examples.hanzi: 他说他一定会成功，我们走着瞧。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō tā yīdìng huì chénggōng, wǒmen zǒuzheqiáo.
examples.english: He says he'll surely succeed, so let's wait and see.

components.note: 米 (rice) — refined grain gives the idea of essence and the best part, hence 精 fine, spirit (精神).
青 (qīng) is a near sound match (-ing); the series 青 清 请 情 晴 静 helps recall jīng.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.
疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound) — as in 险, 阳, 阴: a walled yard.
完 (wán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; also in 玩 wán.

example.hanzi: 他因病情严重被送进了精神病院。
example.pinyin: Tā yīn bìngqíng yánzhòng bèi sòng jìnle jīngshénbìngyuàn.
example.english: Because his condition was severe, he was sent to a mental hospital.
example.fact: Bethlem Royal Hospital in London, founded in 1247, is the oldest continuously operating psychiatric institution in the world, though for centuries it was better known by its nickname 'Bedlam,' a word that eventually entered the English language to mean chaos or confusion. Paying visitors could once view patients there as a form of entertainment, a practice finally banned in the late eighteenth century.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影的故事发生在一家精神病院里。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de gùshi fāshēng zài yī jiā jīngshénbìngyuàn lǐ.
examples.english: The story of this film takes place in a psychiatric hospital.

examples.hanzi: 医生在精神病院工作了二十年。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng zài jīngshénbìngyuàn gōngzuò le èrshí nián.
examples.english: The doctor has worked at the mental hospital for twenty years.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and links, as in 红, 经, 系: thread gathered into one.
充 (chōng) is only a loose sound clue for tǒng.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; counting aloud.
十 (ten) — counting up to ten: 计 is to count and reckon.

example.hanzi: 这份报告需要更详细的统计数据。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào xūyào gèng xiángxì de tǒngjì shùjù.
example.english: This report needs more detailed statistical data.
example.fact: Florence Nightingale, better remembered as a nursing pioneer, was also an accomplished statistician who invented a form of pie chart called the 'coxcomb diagram' to show British military commanders that far more soldiers in the Crimean War were dying of preventable disease than of battle wounds. Her visual statistics helped push through sanitary reforms in army hospitals and later got her elected the first female member of the Royal Statistical Society.

examples.hanzi: 请统计一下今天来了多少人。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng tǒngjì yīxià jīntiān lái le duōshao rén.
examples.english: Please count how many people came today.

examples.hanzi: 根据统计，今年的游客增加了两成。
examples.pinyin: Gēnjù tǒngjì, jīnnián de yóukè zēngjiā le liǎng chéng.
examples.english: According to statistics, tourists increased by twenty percent this year.

components.note: 月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: tasks take effort. The top 夂 stands in for the traditional 務.
Four mouths 口 (vessels) with a dog 犬 guarding them — the traditional explanation; 器 is any vessel or tool, as in 武器 and 机器.

example.hanzi: 网站因为服务器故障暂时无法访问。
example.pinyin: Wǎngzhàn yīnwèi fúwùqì gùzhàng zànshí wúfǎ fǎngwèn.
example.english: The website is temporarily inaccessible due to a server failure.
example.fact: The world's first web server was a NeXT computer built by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in 1990, and it was so central to the fledgling web that a handwritten label on the machine warned colleagues, 'This machine is a server. DO NOT POWER IT DOWN!!' That same physical computer is preserved today at CERN as a historical artifact of the internet's early infrastructure.

examples.hanzi: 服务器太忙了，网页打不开。
examples.pinyin: Fúwùqì tài máng le, wǎngyè dǎ bù kāi.
examples.english: The server is too busy and the page won't open.

examples.hanzi: 公司把数据存放在云服务器上。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī bǎ shùjù cúnfàng zài yún fúwùqì shàng.
examples.english: The company stores data on a cloud server.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 挑 is to pick out by hand.
兆 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 跳 tiào, 桃 táo and 逃 táo.
戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
贝 (cowrie) — money and value, as in 财, 货, 买: competing for prizes was once tied to offerings and stakes.

example.hanzi: 这场机器人挑战赛吸引了上百支队伍参加。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng jīqìrén tiǎozhànsài xīyǐnle shàng bǎi zhī duìwǔ cānjiā.
example.english: This robotics challenge competition attracted more than a hundred teams.
example.fact: The Ansari X Prize, a $10 million challenge competition announced in 1996, offered its prize to the first privately funded team to launch a reusable crewed spacecraft to the edge of space twice within two weeks. Aerospace designer Burt Rutan's SpaceShipOne claimed the prize in 2004, a milestone widely credited with kick-starting the modern private spaceflight industry that later produced companies like Virgin Galactic and Blue Origin.

examples.hanzi: 这个周末有一场城市马拉松挑战赛。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhōumò yǒu yī chǎng chéngshì mǎlāsōng tiǎozhànsài.
examples.english: This weekend there is a city marathon challenge.

examples.hanzi: 他们队在挑战赛中输给了去年的冠军。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen duì zài tiǎozhànsài zhōng shū gěi le qùnián de guànjūn.
examples.english: Their team lost to last year's champions in the challenge match.

components.note: The shape does not explain 与 today (simplified from 與, two hands handing something over). Memory aid: a hand passing a thing along, hence 'give' and then 'and, with'.
此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 他在厨房做饭,与此同时,孩子们在客厅写作业。
example.pinyin: Tā zài chúfáng zuòfàn, yǔcǐtóngshí, háizimen zài kètīng xiě zuòyè.
example.english: He was cooking in the kitchen; meanwhile, the kids were doing homework in the living room.
example.fact: Einstein's theory of special relativity, published in 1905, showed that 'at the same time' isn't an absolute fact about the universe: two events that appear simultaneous to one observer can appear to happen at different times to another observer moving at a different speed. This relativity of simultaneity has been repeatedly confirmed experimentally, including with precise atomic clocks flown on airplanes that tick at measurably different rates than identical clocks left on the ground.

examples.hanzi: 我在开会，与此同时，他在外面等我。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài kāihuì, yǔ cǐ tóngshí, tā zài wàimiàn děng wǒ.
examples.english: I was in the meeting, and meanwhile he was waiting for me outside.

examples.hanzi: 公司的利润上升了，与此同时，成本也在增加。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī de lìrùn shàngshēng le, yǔ cǐ tóngshí, chéngběn yě zài zēngjiā.
examples.english: The company's profits rose, while at the same time costs also increased.

components.note: 肉 (meat) — rotting meat, with the broad cover 广 over it; 肉 also appears as ⺼ in body parts like 脸 face.
付 (fù) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 府 fǔ and 附 fù.
火 (fire) — cooked to mush, then rotten; also in 烧 burn, 灯 lamp.
兰 (lán) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 栏 lán and 拦 lán.

example.hanzi: 冰箱里的水果已经腐烂了。
example.pinyin: Bīngxiāng lǐ de shuǐguǒ yǐjīng fǔlàn le.
example.english: The fruit in the refrigerator has already rotted.
example.fact: Ötzi the Iceman, a naturally mummified body discovered in the Alps in 1991, was preserved for roughly 5,300 years because he died in a spot where snow and ice quickly covered him, cutting off the oxygen and bacterial activity that normally cause organic remains to rot. Researchers have since reconstructed his last meals, tattoos, and even a fatal arrow wound from the remarkably intact tissue.

examples.hanzi: 树叶掉在地上，慢慢腐烂了。
examples.pinyin: Shùyè diào zài dìshàng, mànman fǔlàn le.
examples.english: The leaves fell on the ground and slowly rotted.

examples.hanzi: 这种制度已经腐烂了，必须改革。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zhìdù yǐjīng fǔlàn le, bìxū gǎigé.
examples.english: This system has become corrupt and must be reformed.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 迷; 送 is walking someone off, or delivering.

example.hanzi: 警车一路护送车队通过市区。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchē yīlù hùsòng chēduì tōngguò shìqū.
example.english: Police cars escorted the convoy through the city the whole way.
example.fact: Along the ancient Silk Road, merchant caravans crossing Central Asia often hired armed guards or paid local rulers for safe-passage escorts through dangerous stretches of desert and mountain pass, since bandit raids were a constant risk over the thousands of miles between China and the Mediterranean. Entire towns along the route grew wealthy largely by providing these caravans with escorts, lodging, and fresh pack animals.

examples.hanzi: 警察护送这位证人去了法院。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá hùsòng zhè wèi zhèngrén qù le fǎyuàn.
examples.english: The police escorted the witness to the court.

examples.hanzi: 海军派出军舰护送商船通过海峡。
examples.pinyin: Hǎijūn pàichū jūnjiàn hùsòng shāngchuán tōngguò hǎixiá.
examples.english: The navy sent warships to escort merchant ships through the strait.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: a building holds things.
谷 (valley) — a hollow that holds: 容 is to hold or allow.
Four mouths 口 (vessels) with a dog 犬 guarding them — the traditional explanation; 器 is any vessel or tool, as in 武器 and 机器.

example.hanzi: 请把液体倒进这个容器里。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yètǐ dào jìn zhège róngqì lǐ.
example.english: Please pour the liquid into this container.
example.fact: The modern intermodal shipping container was standardized by American trucking entrepreneur Malcom McLean, who loaded the first commercial container ship, the Ideal-X, in 1956, cutting the cost of loading cargo by roughly 90 percent compared with the old method of hand-loading loose goods. That single standardized steel box is often credited with enabling the scale of global trade seen today, since goods could move seamlessly between ships, trains, and trucks without ever being unpacked.

examples.hanzi: 请用干净的容器装水。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng yòng gānjìng de róngqì zhuāng shuǐ.
examples.english: Please use a clean container for the water.

examples.hanzi: 这些塑料容器可以重复使用。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē sùliào róngqì kěyǐ chóngfù shǐyòng.
examples.english: These plastic containers can be reused.

components.note: 高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.
贝 (shell, old money) — value and price, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy, 费 fee.

example.hanzi: 她穿着一身高贵的礼服出席晚宴。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhuó yī shēn gāoguì de lǐfú chūxí wǎnyàn.
example.english: She wore an elegant, noble gown to attend the evening banquet.
example.fact: The 'noble gases' — helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, and radon — earned their name in chemistry because they almost never react with other elements, much as aristocrats were once imagined to stand aloof from ordinary society. This near-total inertness comes from having a full outer shell of electrons, which leaves them with essentially nothing to gain or lose by bonding, unlike almost every other element on the periodic table.

examples.hanzi: 她举止高贵，像一位公主。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǔzhǐ gāoguì, xiàng yī wèi gōngzhǔ.
examples.english: She carries herself nobly, like a princess.

examples.hanzi: 高贵的品质比财富更重要。
examples.pinyin: Gāoguì de pǐnzhì bǐ cáifù gèng zhòngyào.
examples.english: Noble qualities are more important than wealth.

meanings: to hold a governmental office or post

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱; 担 is to carry on the shoulder, then to bear a duty.
旦 (dàn) is a close sound clue for dān; 旦 also sounds out 但 dàn and 胆 dǎn.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 任 is a duty a person bears.
壬 (rén) gives the same sound, different tone; also in 妊 rèn.

example.hanzi: 他将担任这家公司的首席执行官。
example.pinyin: Tā jiāng dānrèn zhè jiā gōngsī de shǒuxí zhíxíngguān.
example.english: He will serve as this company's chief executive officer.
example.fact: Queen Elizabeth II served as the United Kingdom's monarch for over 70 years, from 1952 until her death in 2022, making her reign the longest of any British monarch and one of the longest of any verified monarch in world history. Over that span she worked with 15 different UK prime ministers, starting with Winston Churchill and ending with Liz Truss.

examples.hanzi: 她担任这个班的班主任已经五年了。
examples.pinyin: Tā dānrèn zhège bān de bānzhǔrèn yǐjīng wǔ nián le.
examples.english: She has been the homeroom teacher of this class for five years.

examples.hanzi: 谁来担任这次活动的主持人？
examples.pinyin: Shéi lái dānrèn zhè cì huódòng de zhǔchírén?
examples.english: Who will host this event?

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 这门课主要讲人体的生理结构。
example.pinyin: Zhè mén kè zhǔyào jiǎng réntǐ de shēnglǐ jiégòu.
example.english: This course mainly covers the physiological structure of the human body.
example.fact: English physician William Harvey demonstrated in his 1628 work 'De Motu Cordis' that blood circulates continuously through the body in one direction, pumped by the heart, overturning the ancient Greek belief that blood was newly generated by the liver and simply consumed by the tissues. He calculated that the heart pumps far more blood in an hour than the body could possibly manufacture that quickly, strong indirect evidence for circulation offered decades before microscopes could actually see capillaries.

examples.hanzi: 青春期孩子的生理变化很明显。
examples.pinyin: Qīngchūnqī háizi de shēnglǐ biànhuà hěn míngxiǎn.
examples.english: Physiological changes in teenagers are obvious.

examples.hanzi: 睡眠是人类生理上的基本需求。
examples.pinyin: Shuìmián shì rénlèi shēnglǐ shàng de jīběn xūqiú.
examples.english: Sleep is a basic physiological need of humans.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — marks bows and stretching, as in 张, 引, 弯; 弥 is to fill or extend.
尔 (ěr) is only a loose hint for mí.

example.hanzi: 他想弥补自己的错误。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng míbǔ zìjǐ de cuòwù.
example.english: He wants to make up for his mistake.
example.fact: 弥 appears in 弥补 (make up for), 弥漫 (to spread), 弥天大谎 (a whopping lie). 阿弥陀佛 is the Buddhist invocation.

examples.hanzi: 这个办法可以弥补我们的损失。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ kěyǐ míbǔ wǒmen de sǔnshī.
examples.english: This method can make up for our losses.

examples.hanzi: 房间里弥漫着一股花香。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ mímàn zhe yì gǔ huāxiāng.
examples.english: A floral scent filled the room.

components.note: 见 (see) — 靓 is pretty to look at, as in 靓女; 青 hints at youth and freshness.
青 (qīng) — loose sound hint (liàng/jìng vs qīng).

example.hanzi: 她今天穿得很靓。
example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān chuān de hěn liàng.
example.english: She's dressed beautifully today.
example.fact: 靓 comes from Cantonese 靚. 靓仔 is 'handsome guy' and 靓女 'pretty girl', 靓丽 means beautiful. The old dictionary reading jìng is now rare.

examples.hanzi: 这个女孩儿真靓，大家都喜欢她。
examples.pinyin: Zhège nǚháir zhēn liàng, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan tā.
examples.english: This girl is so pretty that everyone likes her.

examples.hanzi: 你的新发型真靓！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de xīn fàxíng zhēn liàng!
examples.english: Your new hairstyle looks great!

components.note: 束 (bind) — a 木 tied around with a cord 口: a bundle of wood. 束 also gives 速 sù (hurried) and 嗽 sòu.

example.hanzi: 他送了我一束花。
example.pinyin: Tā sòng le wǒ yí shù huā.
example.english: He gave me a bunch of flowers.
example.fact: 束 is a measure word for flowers, beams of light and bundles: 一束花, 一束光. It is also in 结束 (finish), 约束 (restrain) and 束缚 (to bind).

examples.hanzi: 他把玫瑰花扎成了一束送给妈妈。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ méiguihuā zā chéng le yí shù sòng gěi māma.
examples.english: He tied the flowers into a bunch.

examples.hanzi: 比赛结束了，大家都回家了。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài jiéshù le, dàjiā dōu huí jiā le.
examples.english: The match ended and everyone went home.

components.note: 讠 (speech; traditional 言) — marks speaking and language, as in 说 say, 话 speech, 请 request; 诶 is an interjection of surprise.
矣 (yǐ) — loose sound hint (ēi vs yǐ).

example.hanzi: 诶，你看那边！
example.pinyin: Ēi, nǐ kàn nàbiān!
example.english: Hey, look over there!
example.fact: 诶 is a written form of 欸, an interjection that changes meaning with tone: ēi (hey), éi (huh?), ěi (what?) and èi (yes). It's most common in chat and informal writing.

examples.hanzi: 诶，你怎么还在这儿？
examples.pinyin: Éi, nǐ zěnme hái zài zhèr?
examples.english: Hey, why are you still here?

examples.hanzi: 诶？这不是我的手机吗？
examples.pinyin: Éi? Zhè búshì wǒ de shǒujī ma?
examples.english: Huh? Isn't this my book?

components.note: 彳 (step) — walking and conduct, as in 行, 往, 得, 很.
聿 (brush) — writing the rules: 律 is law, and a rule of rhythm.

example.hanzi: 你应该遵守法律。
example.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi zūnshǒu fǎlǜ.
example.english: You should obey the law.
example.fact: 律 gives 法律 (law), 律师 (lawyer), 纪律 (discipline), 规律 (pattern), 一律 (all alike) and 旋律 (melody).

examples.hanzi: 这家公司请了一位律师。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī qǐng le yí wèi lǜshī.
examples.english: This company hired a lawyer.

examples.hanzi: 他每天过着很规律的生活。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān guò zhe hěn guīlǜ de shēnghuó.
examples.english: He lives a very regular life every day.

components.note: 穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.
白 (white, bright) — gives sound to 拍 pāi, 怕 pà, 伯 bó and 泊 bó. Meaning: white, clear, plain, hence "明白" understand.

example.hanzi: 请在表格的空白处填写你的姓名。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài biǎogé de kòngbái chù tiánxiě nǐ de xìngmíng.
example.english: Please fill in your name in the blank space on the form.
example.fact: Medieval European mapmakers often left unexplored regions blank or filled them with the warning phrase 'hic sunt dracones' — 'here be dragons' — marking the edges of known geography rather than guessing at what lay beyond. Explorers' voyages gradually filled in these blank spaces over the centuries, and by the early twentieth century, cartographers had mapped nearly the entire globe, leaving few blank areas beyond the poles and ocean depths.

examples.hanzi: 这页纸是空白的，什么都没写。
examples.pinyin: Zhè yè zhǐ shì kòngbái de, shénme dōu méi xiě.
examples.english: This page is blank, with nothing written on it.

examples.hanzi: 我的脑子一片空白，什么也想不起来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de nǎozi yī piàn kòngbái, shénme yě xiǎng bù qǐlái.
examples.english: My mind went blank and I couldn't remember anything.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.

example.hanzi: 学生们努力练习正确的发音。
example.pinyin: xuéshengmen nǔlì liànxí zhèngquè de fāyīn.
example.english: The students work hard to practice correct pronunciation.
example.fact: The human vocal folds vibrate somewhere between 100 and 1,000 times per second to generate the raw pitch behind speech, and it's the vocal tract's shaping of that airflow — the tongue, teeth, and lips working together — that turns vibration into recognizable words. Songbirds do something similar with a specialized organ called a syrinx, which lets them produce two independent pitches at once, something no human vocal tract can manage.

examples.hanzi: 你的发音很标准，一点口音也没有。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de fāyīn hěn biāozhǔn, yīdiǎn kǒuyīn yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: Your pronunciation is very standard, with no accent at all.

examples.hanzi: 这个字有两种发音，意思也不同。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zì yǒu liǎng zhǒng fāyīn, yìsi yě bùtóng.
examples.english: This character has two pronunciations with different meanings.

components.note: 穴 (cave, hole) — creeping in through a hole; also in 空 empty, 窗 window.
切 (qiè) gives the exact sound.
口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.
Four mouths 口 (vessels) with a dog 犬 guarding them — the traditional explanation; 器 is any vessel or tool, as in 武器 and 机器.

example.hanzi: 警方在办公室里发现了一个窃听器。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng zài bàngōngshì lǐ fāxiàn le yí gè qiètīngqì.
example.english: Police discovered a bug in the office.
example.fact: In 1945, Soviet schoolchildren gave the US ambassador in Moscow a carved wooden Great Seal of the United States as a gift of friendship; hidden inside was a passive listening device — nicknamed "The Thing" — that needed no battery or wiring and went undetected for seven years, quietly relaying conversations from the ambassador's own study.

examples.hanzi: 他怀疑自己的手机里被装了窃听器。
examples.pinyin: Tā huáiyí zìjǐ de shǒujī lǐ bèi zhuāng le qiètīngqì.
examples.english: He suspects a bugging device was installed in his phone.

examples.hanzi: 侦探在电话线上发现了一个小窃听器。
examples.pinyin: Zhēntàn zài diànhuà xiàn shàng fāxiàn le yī gè xiǎo qiètīngqì.
examples.english: The detective found a small bug on the telephone line.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and joining, as in 听, 聪, 闻: 联 first meant ears joined, so to link. The part 关 stands in for the traditional shape.
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.hanzi: 联合国总部设在纽约市。
example.pinyin: Liánhéguó zǒngbù shè zài Niǔyuē Shì.
example.english: The United Nations headquarters is located in New York City.
example.fact: The United Nations was founded in San Francisco in 1945 by 51 countries in the aftermath of World War II. Its Manhattan headquarters sits on land purchased with an $8.5 million donation from John D. Rockefeller Jr., and the site is technically international territory rather than part of the United States.

examples.hanzi: 联合国呼吁各国共同保护环境。
examples.pinyin: Liánhéguó hūyù gè guó gòngtóng bǎohù huánjìng.
examples.english: The United Nations calls on all countries to protect the environment together.

examples.hanzi: 她在联合国担任翻译工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài Liánhéguó dānrèn fānyì gōngzuò.
examples.english: She works as an interpreter at the United Nations.
